title.en: Volume 160 Biographies 85: Xu, Lu, Meng, Liu, Yang, Pan, Cui, Wei
title.raw: 卷一百六十 列傳第八十五 徐呂孟劉楊潘崔韋 Volume 160 Biographies 85: Xu, Lu, Meng, Liu, Yang, Pan, Cui, Wei

sentences.zh: 徐呂孟劉楊潘崔韋

translations.literal: Xu, Lu, Meng, Liu, Yang, Pan, Cui, Wei
translations.idiomatic: Xu, Lu, Meng, Liu, Yang, Pan, Cui, and Wei

sentences.zh: 5.2.1 淩子 敬之

translations.literal: 5.2.1 Lingzi Jingzhi
translations.idiomatic: 5.2.1: Jingzhi, son of Ling

translations.literal: 7.1.1 Son Hang
translations.idiomatic: 7.1.1: His son Hang

sentences.zh: 徐浩，字季海，越州人。

translations.literal: Xu Hao, styled Jihai, was a man of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Hao, whose style name was Jihai, came from Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 擢明經，有文辭。

translations.literal: He was selected through the Mingjing examination and possessed literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Mingjing examination and showed a gift for writing.

sentences.zh: 張說稱其才，由魯山主簿薦為集賢校理，見《喜雨》、《五色鴿賦》，咨嗟曰：「後來之英也！

translations.literal: Zhang Yue praised his talent; from his post as master of records at Lushan he was recommended as collator of the Hall of Assembled Eminences. When Zhang saw the 《Ode on Joy in Rain》 and the 《Ode on the Five-Colored Dove》, he sighed in admiration and said: "A talent of the coming generation!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue spoke highly of his ability, and on his recommendation from the post of chief clerk at Lushan he was made collator in the Hall of Assembled Eminences. Reading Hao's 《Ode on Joy in Rain》 and 《Ode on the Five-Colored Dove》, Zhang exclaimed with admiration: "Here is a champion of the next age!

sentences.zh: 」進監察御史裏行。

translations.literal: " He was advanced to attendant censor-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao was then promoted to attendant censor-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 辟幽州張守珪幕府。

translations.literal: He was invited to Zhang Shougui's staff in Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the military staff of Zhang Shougui in Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 歷河陽令，治有績。

translations.literal: He served in succession as magistrate of Heyang, where his administration achieved results.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Heyang, where his governance won a solid record.

sentences.zh: 東都留守王倕表署其府。

translations.literal: Wang Wei, military governor of the eastern capital, memorialized to appoint him to his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wei, who held the eastern capital as military governor, summoned him to his staff by memorial.

sentences.zh: 民有妄作符命者，眾不為疑，浩獨按篆詰狀，果詐為之。

translations.literal: Among the people was one who falsely fabricated inscribed talismans; the crowd did not suspect him, but Hao alone examined the seal script and interrogated the case—it proved to be a forgery.
translations.idiomatic: When a commoner forged prophetic inscriptions, the public took him at face value, but Hao alone scrutinized the seal script and pressed the case, proving the documents fraudulent.

sentences.zh: 遷累都官郎中，為嶺南選補使，又領東都選。

translations.literal: He was transferred through several posts to director of the Bureau of Reviews, served as commissioner for selection and appointment in Lingnan, and also oversaw selection for the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several offices to director of the Bureau of Reviews, served as commissioner for appointments in Lingnan, and also headed the eastern-capital selection board.

sentences.zh: 肅宗立，由襄州刺史召授中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong acceded, Hao was summoned from his post as prefect of Xiangzhou and appointed Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Suzong took the throne, Hao was recalled from the prefecture of Xiang and made Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 四方詔令，多出浩手，遣辭贍速，而書法至精，帝喜之。

translations.literal: Edicts from all quarters were mostly drafted by Hao; his phrasing was rich and swift, and his calligraphy was of the utmost refinement—the emperor delighted in him.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial proclamations from every direction largely passed through Hao's hand—his wording was ample and swift, his brushwork exquisite—and the emperor took great pleasure in him.

sentences.zh: 又參太上皇誥冊，寵絕一時。

translations.literal: He also took part in drafting the retired emperor's edicts and patents, and his favor at court surpassed all others of the time.
translations.idiomatic: He also helped compose the retired emperor's edicts and enfeoffment patents, and for a time no one at court enjoyed greater favor.

sentences.zh: 授兼尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He was granted the additional title of Vice Director of the Right of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the concurrent post of Vice Director of the Right in the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 浩建言：「故事，有司斷獄，必刑部審覆。

translations.literal: Hao submitted a proposal: "By established practice, whenever a bureau pronounced judgment in a criminal case, the Ministry of Justice had to review and confirm it.
translations.idiomatic: Hao memorialized: "Under long-standing precedent, whenever a department rendered judgment in a criminal case, the Ministry of Justice had to review and confirm the sentence.

sentences.zh: 自李林甫、楊國忠當國，專作威福，許有司就宰相府斷事，尚書以下，未省即署，乖慎恤意。

translations.literal: Since Li Linfu and Yang Guozhong held sway, they monopolized power and patronage, allowing bureaus to render judgments at the chancellor's office; the Director and below would affix their seals without even examining the cases—a departure from cautious, compassionate intent.
translations.idiomatic: Since Li Linfu and Yang Guozhong dominated the government, arrogating power and favors, departments were allowed to decide cases at the chancellor's residence; directors and below would seal documents without even reading them—contrary to the spirit of careful, compassionate justice.

sentences.zh: 請如故便。

translations.literal: I request that the former practice be restored for convenience.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the former practice be restored as before.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: " The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 故詳斷復自此始。

translations.literal: Thus detailed review and judgment began again from this point.
translations.idiomatic: From this time onward, full review of verdicts was restored.

sentences.zh: 進國子祭酒，為李輔國譖，貶廬州長史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, but was slandered by Li Fuguo and demoted to Long Prefect of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, but Li Fuguo slandered him and he was demoted to Long Prefect of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 代宗復以中書舍人召，遷工部侍郎、會稽縣公，出為嶺南節度使。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong again summoned him as Attendant of the Secretariat, promoted him to Vice Minister of Works and Duke of Kuaiji, and sent him out as military governor of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong recalled him again as Attendant of the Secretariat, promoted him to Vice Minister of Works and Duke of Kuaiji, then sent him out as military governor of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 召拜吏部侍郎，與薛邕分典選。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Personnel, sharing charge of selection with Xue Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed Vice Minister of Personnel, sharing oversight of the civil-service examinations with Xue Yong.

sentences.zh: 浩有妾弟冒優，托之邕，擬長安尉，御史大夫李棲筠劾之，帝怒，黜邕歙州刺史，浩明州別駕。

translations.literal: Hao had a younger brother by a concubine who fraudulently claimed seniority in the rankings and entrusted the matter to Yong, who nominated him for the post of sheriff of Chang'an. The Censor-in-Chief Li Qiyun impeached them; the emperor was furious and demoted Yong to Prefect of Shezhou and Hao to assistant prefect of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's younger half-brother falsely claimed examination precedence and asked Yong to secure him the Chang'an sheriffcy; Censor-in-Chief Li Qiyun impeached them. The emperor was enraged and demoted Yong to prefect of Shezhou and Hao to assistant prefect of Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 德宗初，召授彭王傅，進郡公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Dezong's reign, Hao was summoned and appointed Tutor of the Prince of Peng, and promoted to a commandery duke.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dezong's reign he was recalled and made Tutor of the Prince of Peng, advancing to commandery duke.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十，贈太子少師，謚曰定。

translations.literal: He died at eighty; posthumously he was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty; posthumously he was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous epithet Ding.

sentences.zh: 始，浩父嶠之善書，以法授浩，益工。

translations.literal: At the outset, Hao's father Xu Qiao had excelled at calligraphy and passed on the method to Hao, who became still more accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: From the first, Hao's father Xu Qiao had been skilled at calligraphy and taught him the art; Hao surpassed him.

sentences.zh: 嘗書四十二幅屏，八體皆備，草隸尤工，世狀其法曰「怒猊抉石，渴驥奔泉」雲。

translations.literal: Once he wrote forty-two screen panels in eight scripts, all complete; his grass and clerical scripts were especially fine. Later ages described his style as "an enraged lion tearing stone, a thirsty stallion rushing to a spring."
translations.idiomatic: He once filled forty-two screen panels, mastering all eight scripts; his cursive and clerical hands were especially fine. Later generations described his brush as "a furious lion clawing stone, a thirsty steed racing to a spring."

sentences.zh: 晚節治廣及領選，頗嗜財，惑於所嬖，卒以敗。

translations.literal: In his later years, while administering Guangzhou and overseeing selection, he came to covet wealth greatly and was misled by his favorites, and in the end met ruin.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years, governing Guangzhou and heading the selection boards, he grew greedy for wealth and was led astray by his favorites, and in the end was ruined.

sentences.zh: 呂渭，字君載，河中人。

translations.literal: Lu Wei, styled Junzai, was a man of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wei, whose style name was Junzai, came from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 父延之，終浙東節度使。

translations.literal: His father Yanzhi served to the end as military governor of Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yanzhi ended his career as military governor of Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 渭第進士，從浙西觀察使李涵為支使，進殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Wei passed the jinshi examination and followed Li Han, commissioner of the Zhexi circuit, as a branch secretary; he was promoted to palace attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: Wei passed the jinshi examination, served Li Han, commissioner of Zhexi, as a branch secretary, and was promoted to palace attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 大歷末，涵為元陵副使，渭又為判官。

translations.literal: At the end of the Dali reign, Han served as deputy commissioner for the Yuanling works, and Wei again served as his administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Dali era Han became deputy commissioner for the Yuanling mausoleum works, and Wei again served as his aide.

sentences.zh: 涵由御史大夫擢太子少傅，渭建言：「涵父名少康，當避。

translations.literal: When Han was promoted from Censor-in-Chief to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Wei submitted a memorial: "Han's father's given name was Shaokang; taboo should be observed.
translations.idiomatic: When Han rose from Censor-in-Chief to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Wei memorialized: "Han's father's given name was Shaokang; the taboo should be observed.

sentences.zh: 」宰相崔祐甫善其言，擢司門員外郎。

translations.literal: " The chancellor Cui Youfu approved his words and promoted him to Vice Director of the Gate.
translations.idiomatic: " Chancellor Cui Youfu approved the argument and promoted Wei to Vice Director of the Gate.

sentences.zh: 御史共劾渭：「昔涵再任少卿，不以嫌，今謂少傅為慢官，疑渭為涵遊說。

translations.literal: The censors jointly impeached Wei: "In the past Han twice held the post of Vice Chamberlain without Wei citing taboo; now he calls the Junior Tutor post a slight office and suspects Wei of lobbying on Han's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: The censors jointly impeached Wei: "Earlier Han twice held Vice Chamberlain without Wei raising taboo; now he calls the Junior Tutor a slight post—one suspects Wei was lobbying for Han.

sentences.zh: 」乃貶渭歙州司馬。

translations.literal: " Wei was therefore demoted to Sima of Shezhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Wei was demoted to Sima of Shezhou.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，累遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: During the Zhenyuan period he was promoted through several posts to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenyuan era he rose through several offices to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 始，中書省有古柳，建中末枯死，德宗自梁還，復榮茂，人以為瑞柳，渭令貢士賦之。

translations.literal: Originally there had been an ancient willow in the Secretariat; at the end of the Jianzhong era it withered and died. When Dezong returned from Liang, it flourished again with lush foliage. People regarded it as an auspicious willow. Wei ordered the examination candidates to compose rhapsodies on it.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago an ancient willow stood in the Secretariat; it withered at the end of Jianzhong. When Dezong returned from Liang it flourished anew, and people hailed it as an auspicious willow. Wei ordered examination candidates to compose rhapsodies on the tree.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，不以為善。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of this, he did not regard it as good.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it, he was displeased.

sentences.zh: 又與裴延齡為姻家，擢其子操上第，會入閣，遺私謁之書於廷。

translations.literal: He was also related by marriage to Pei Yanling and promoted his son Cao to top rank of the examination; when Cao entered the inner court, he left on the floor a private letter seeking audience.
translations.idiomatic: He was also related by marriage to Pei Yanling and placed his son Cao at the head of the examination list; when Cao entered the inner court he dropped a private petition for audience on the floor.

sentences.zh: 出為潭州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as prefect of Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈陜州大都督。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Grand Protector-General of Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Grand Protector-General of Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 四子：溫、恭、儉、讓。

translations.literal: Four sons: Wen, Gong, Jian, and Rang.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Wen, Gong, Jian, and Rang.

sentences.zh: 子 溫

translations.literal: Son Wen
translations.idiomatic: His son Wen

sentences.zh: 溫，字和叔，一字化光，從陸質治《春秋》，梁肅為文章。

translations.literal: Wen, styled Heqi, also known by the courtesy name Huaguang, studied the Spring and Autumn Annals under Lu Zhi, and prose composition under Liang Su.
translations.idiomatic: Wen, styled Heqi and also known as Huaguang, studied the Spring and Autumn Annals under Lu Zhi and literary composition under Liang Su.

sentences.zh: 貞元末，擢進士第。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhenyuan era he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Zhenyuan era he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 與韋執誼厚，因善王叔文。

translations.literal: He was close to Wei Zhiyi and through that friendship became intimate with Wang Shuwen.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Wei Zhiyi and through him became intimate with Wang Shuwen.

sentences.zh: 再遷為左拾遺。

translations.literal: He was twice promoted to Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: He was twice promoted to Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 以侍御史副張薦使吐蕃，會順宗立，薦卒於虜，虜以中國有喪，留溫不遣。

translations.literal: As vice censor he accompanied Zhang Jian on an embassy to Tibet; when Emperor Shunzong acceded, Jian died in the foreign land. The Tibetans, noting that China was in mourning, detained Wen and would not let him return.
translations.idiomatic: As vice censor he accompanied Zhang Jian on an embassy to Tibet; when Emperor Shunzong acceded, Jian died among the barbarians. The Tibetans, seeing that the court was in mourning, detained Wen and refused to release him.

sentences.zh: 時叔文秉權，與遊者皆貴顯，溫在絕域不得遷，常自悲。

translations.literal: At that time Shuwen held power, and all who associated with him were honored and elevated; Wen remained in a distant land and could not be promoted, and often grieved on his own account.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Shuwen held power and his associates all rose to eminence, while Wen languished in a distant land unable to advance, and often grieved alone.

sentences.zh: 元和元年乃還，而柳宗元等皆坐叔文貶，溫獨免，進戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhe he at last returned, while Liu Zongyuan and others were all punished for association with Shuwen and banished; Wen alone was spared and promoted to Vice Director of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanhe he finally returned; Liu Zongyuan and others were all punished for ties to Shuwen and banished, but Wen alone was spared and made Vice Director of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 溫操翰精富，一時流輩推尚。

translations.literal: Wen was skilled and prolific in literary composition, and men of the age ranked him among the foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Wen wielded the brush with skill and abundance, and contemporaries held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 性險躁，譎詭而好利，與竇群、羊士諤相昵。

translations.literal: His disposition was dangerous and rash, crafty and deceptive yet greedy for gain; he was intimate with Dou Qun and Yang Shiyi.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was treacherous and impetuous, cunning and greedy; he was close to Dou Qun and Yang Shiyi.

sentences.zh: 群為御史中丞，薦溫知雜事，士諤為御史，宰相李吉甫持之，久不報，溫等怨。

translations.literal: When Qun became Vice Censor-in-Chief he recommended Wen to manage miscellaneous affairs; Shiyi became a censor. The chancellor Li Jifu held firm against this, and for a long time no reply was issued; Wen and the others harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When Qun became Vice Censor-in-Chief he recommended Wen to handle miscellaneous affairs and Shiyi for a censor's post; Chancellor Li Jifu blocked the appointments, and after long delay with no answer Wen and his circle grew resentful.

sentences.zh: 時吉甫為宦侍所抑，溫乘其間謀逐之。

translations.literal: At that time Jifu was being suppressed by eunuch attendants; Wen seized the interval to plot his removal.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu was then being pressed by eunuch attendants, and Wen seized the moment to plot his downfall.

sentences.zh: 會吉甫病，夜召術士宿於第，即捕士掠訊，且奏吉甫陰事。

translations.literal: When Jifu fell ill, Wen summoned diviners overnight to his residence, then seized the men, interrogated them under torture, and memorialized Jifu's secret affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Jifu fell ill, Wen had diviners summoned to his house at night, then arrested them and tortured them for testimony, memorializing Jifu's hidden conduct.

sentences.zh: 憲宗駭異，既詰辯，皆妄言，將悉誅群等，吉甫苦救乃免，於是貶溫均州刺史，士諤資州。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong was alarmed and astonished; after cross-examination all proved to be false speech. He was about to execute Qun and the others to the last man, but Jifu strenuously pleaded and they were spared; Wen was then demoted to prefect of Junzhou and Shiyi to Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong was shocked; under questioning all proved false. He was about to execute Qun and the rest outright, but Jifu pleaded strenuously and they were spared; Wen was demoted to prefect of Junzhou and Shiyi to Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 議者不厭，再貶為道州。

translations.literal: Critics were still not satisfied, and he was demoted again to Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion was still unsatisfied, and he was demoted again to Daozhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，徙衡州，治有善狀。

translations.literal: After a long while he was transferred to Hengzhou, where his administration showed fine results.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was transferred to Hengzhou, where his governance earned a good reputation.

sentences.zh: 卒，年四十。

translations.literal: He died at forty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of forty.

sentences.zh: 子 恭

translations.literal: Son Gong
translations.idiomatic: His son Gong

sentences.zh: 恭，字恭叔，尚氣節，喜縱橫、孫吳術。

translations.literal: Gong, styled Gongshu, prized integrity and honor, and delighted in coalitionist strategy and Sun Wu's military methods.
translations.idiomatic: Gong, styled Gongshu, valued integrity and delighted in coalition diplomacy and Sun Wu's military arts.

sentences.zh: 為山南西道府掌書記，進殿中侍御史，終嶺南府判官。

translations.literal: He served as headquarters secretary for the Shanxi circuit, was promoted to palace attendant censor, and ended his career as administrative aide to the Lingnan headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He served as headquarters secretary on the Shanxi West circuit staff, rose to palace attendant censor, and ended as administrative aide on the Lingnan staff.

sentences.zh: 子 儉

translations.literal: Son Jian
translations.idiomatic: His son Jian

sentences.zh: 儉亦為御史。

translations.literal: Jian also served as a censor.
translations.idiomatic: Jian also served as a censor.

sentences.zh: 子 讓

translations.literal: Son Rang
translations.idiomatic: His son Rang

sentences.zh: 讓，太子右庶子。

translations.literal: Rang served as Right Vice Counselor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Rang served as Right Vice Counselor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 皆美材。

translations.literal: All were men of fine talent.
translations.idiomatic: All were men of outstanding ability.

sentences.zh: 孟簡，字幾道，德州平昌人。

translations.literal: Meng Jian, styled Jidao, was a man of Pingchang in Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Jian, whose style name was Jidao, came from Pingchang in Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖詵，武後時同州刺史。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Shen had served as prefect of Tongzhou in Empress Wu's time.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shen had been prefect of Tongzhou under Empress Wu.

sentences.zh: 簡舉進士、宏辭連中，累遷倉部員外郎。

translations.literal: Jian passed both the jinshi and the hongci examinations in succession and was promoted through several posts to Vice Director of the Granary.
translations.idiomatic: Jian passed the jinshi and hongci examinations in succession and rose through several offices to Vice Director of the Granary.

sentences.zh: 王叔文任戶部，簡以不附離見疾，不敢顯黜，宰相韋執誼為徙它曹。

translations.literal: When Wang Shuwen took charge of the Revenue Bureau, Jian was disliked for not joining him and was not openly dismissed; the chancellor Wei Zhiyi transferred him to another bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shuwen took charge of the Revenue Bureau, Jian was resented for refusing to join him; the court did not dare dismiss him openly, and Chancellor Wei Zhiyi transferred him to another office.

sentences.zh: 元和中，拜諫議大夫，知匭事。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe period he was appointed Remonstrance Official and placed in charge of the suggestion box.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanhe he was made Remonstrance Official and put in charge of the suggestion box.

sentences.zh: 韓泰、韓曄之復刺史，吐突承璀為招討使，簡皆固爭，詣延英言不可狀，以悻切出為常州刺史。

translations.literal: When Han Tai and Han Ye were restored as prefects and Tu Tu Chengcui was made campaign commissioner, Jian firmly opposed each measure, going to the Yanying Hall to state in detail why it could not be done; for his blunt severity he was sent out as prefect of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Tai and Han Ye were restored as prefects and Tu Tu Chengcui was made campaign commissioner, Jian opposed each appointment, going to the Yanying Hall to argue at length why they could not stand; for his blunt severity he was sent out as prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 州有孟瀆，久淤閼，簡治導，溉田凡四千頃，以勞賜金紫，召為給事中。

translations.literal: The prefecture had the Meng Sluice, long silted and blocked; Jian dredged and channeled it, irrigating altogether four thousand qing of fields. For this labor he was granted gold-and-purple insignia and summoned as Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture had the Meng Sluice, long choked with silt; Jian dredged and opened it, irrigating four thousand qing of fields. For this service he was granted gold-and-purple insignia and recalled as Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 代李遜為浙東觀察使。

translations.literal: He replaced Li Xun as commissioner of the Zhedong circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He replaced Li Xun as commissioner of Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 遜抑士族，右編人，至橫恣不檢，及簡，一反之，農估兼受其弊，時謂兩失之。

translations.literal: Xun had suppressed the gentry and favored commoners, to the point of lawless arrogance without restraint. When Jian took over, he reversed everything; farmers and merchants both suffered harm—of the age it was said that both had failed.
translations.idiomatic: Xun had suppressed the gentry and favored commoners until they grew lawless and unrestrained; Jian reversed every policy, and farmers and merchants alike suffered—men of the time said both had failed.

sentences.zh: 以工部侍郎召還。

translations.literal: He was summoned back as Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 初，使府得代，詔至，署留後即行。

translations.literal: Initially, when a commissioner received his replacement, upon arrival of the edict he would sign as acting commissioner and depart at once.
translations.idiomatic: Originally, when a commissioner was replaced, as soon as the edict arrived he would sign as acting commissioner and depart immediately.

sentences.zh: 李翛觀察浙西，始請留故使交政。

translations.literal: Li Xun, commissioner of Zhexi, was the first to request that the outgoing commissioner hand over administration.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun, commissioner of Zhexi, was the first to ask that the outgoing commissioner remain to hand over affairs.

sentences.zh: 及簡還半道堂牒還之，如例，乃聽解。

translations.literal: When Jian was returning, halfway through his journey he sent back the headquarters bulletin ordering return, following precedent; only then was dismissal permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian was returning, halfway on the road he sent back a headquarters order for recall, following precedent; only then was he allowed to leave office.

sentences.zh: 進戶部，加御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Minister of Revenue and given the additional title of Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Revenue with the additional title of Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 戶部有二員，判使案者居別一署，謂之「左戶」，元和後，選委華重，宰相多由此進。

translations.literal: The Revenue Ministry had two incumbents; whoever handled the commissioner's desk sat in a separate office called the "Left Revenue." After the Yuanhe period the post commanded splendid weight, and many chancellors rose from it.
translations.idiomatic: The Revenue Ministry had two incumbents; whoever handled the commissioner's portfolio sat in a separate office called the "Left Revenue." After Yuanhe the post carried great prestige, and many chancellors rose from it.

sentences.zh: 崔群既相，而簡代之，故簡意且柄任。

translations.literal: When Cui Qun became chancellor, Jian replaced him; therefore Jian expected he would soon wield the helm.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Qun became chancellor, Jian replaced him in the ministry, and Jian expected he would soon hold the reins of power.

sentences.zh: 及出山南東道節度使，內不樂。

translations.literal: When he was instead sent out as military governor of the Shanxi Dong circuit, inwardly he was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When he was sent out instead as military governor of the Shanxi East circuit, he was inwardly displeased.

sentences.zh: 政頗嚴峭。

translations.literal: His administration was rather severe and stern.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was notably severe.

sentences.zh: 時有詔置臨漢監以牧馬，命簡兼使職。

translations.literal: At the time there was an edict establishing the Linhan Pasturage Office to manage horses, and Jian was ordered to hold the additional commission.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then established the Linhan Pasturage Office to manage horses, and Jian was ordered to hold that additional post.

sentences.zh: 簡以親吏陸翰主奏邸，關通閹侍，翰持之，數傲很，簡怒，追還，以土囊斃之。

translations.literal: Jian had a close subordinate Lu Han oversee the memorial office and maintain relations with eunuch attendants. Han leveraged this position and repeatedly showed arrogance and stubbornness. Jian grew angry, recalled him, and smothered him to death with a bag of earth.
translations.idiomatic: Jian put his trusted clerk Lu Han in charge of the memorial office to maintain ties with eunuch attendants; Han used the post and repeatedly showed arrogance. Jian grew furious, recalled him, and smothered him with a bag of earth.

sentences.zh: 家上變，發簡奸贓，御史劾驗，得遺吐突承璀資七百萬。

translations.literal: Han's family lodged a capital complaint exposing Jian's corruption and bribery; the censors investigated and verified that he had paid Tu Tu Chengcui a bribe of seven million.
translations.idiomatic: Han's family lodged a capital complaint exposing Jian's corruption; censors investigated and found he had paid Tu Tu Chengcui seven million in bribes.

sentences.zh: 左授太子賓客，分司東都，再貶吉州司馬。

translations.literal: He was demoted to left position as guest of the Heir Apparent, stationed at the eastern capital, then demoted again to Sima of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to Guest of the Heir Apparent with duty at the eastern capital, then demoted again to Sima of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 以赦令進睦州刺史，復徙常州，仍太子賓客分司，卒。

translations.literal: By amnesty he was promoted to prefect of Muzhou, then transferred again to Changzhou, still as guest of the Heir Apparent at the eastern capital station, and died.
translations.idiomatic: By amnesty he was promoted to prefect of Muzhou, then transferred again to Changzhou, still serving as Guest of the Heir Apparent at the eastern capital, and died.

sentences.zh: 簡尤工詩，聞江、淮間。

translations.literal: Jian was especially accomplished in poetry, renowned throughout the Jiang and Huai regions.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was especially skilled in poetry and was known throughout the Jiang and Huai regions.

sentences.zh: 尚節義，與之交者，雖歿，視恤其孤不少衰。

translations.literal: He valued righteousness; toward those with whom he had formed bonds, even after their death he did not slacken in caring for their orphans.
translations.idiomatic: He prized integrity; toward friends, even after their death he did not slacken in caring for their orphans.

sentences.zh: 晚路殊躁急，佞佛過甚，為時所誚。

translations.literal: In his later course he became exceptionally rash and impatient, and his excessive devotion to Buddhism drew the ridicule of the age.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he grew exceptionally rash and excessively devoted to Buddhism, drawing the ridicule of his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 嘗與劉伯芻、歸登、蕭俯譯次梵言者。

translations.literal: He once worked with Liu Bochu, Gui Deng, and Xiao Fu on arranging translations of Sanskrit.
translations.idiomatic: He once collaborated with Liu Bochu, Gui Deng, and Xiao Fu on arranging translations of Buddhist Sanskrit texts.

sentences.zh: 劉伯芻

translations.literal: Liu Bochu
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bochu

sentences.zh: 劉伯芻，字素芝，兵部侍郎迺之子。

translations.literal: Liu Bochu, styled Suzhi, was the son of the Vice Minister of War Liu Nai.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bochu, whose style name was Suzhi, was the son of Vice Minister of War Liu Nai.

sentences.zh: 行修謹。

translations.literal: His conduct was cultivated and careful.
translations.idiomatic: His conduct was cultivated and careful.

sentences.zh: 淮南杜佑奏署節度府判官。

translations.literal: Du You of Huainan memorialized to appoint him administrative aide on the military governor's staff.
translations.idiomatic: Du You of Huainan had him appointed administrative aide on the circuit staff.

sentences.zh: 府罷，召拜右補闕，遷主客員外郎。

translations.literal: When the headquarters was dissolved, he was summoned and appointed Right Reminder, then promoted to Vice Director of Guests.
translations.idiomatic: When the staff was disbanded, he was recalled as Right Reminder and promoted to Vice Director of Guests.

sentences.zh: 數過友家飲噱，為韋執誼陰劾，貶虔州參軍。

translations.literal: He often visited friends' homes for drinking and jesting and was secretly impeached by Wei Zhiyi, demoted to military adjutant of Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He often visited friends for drinking and banter; Wei Zhiyi impeached him in secret and he was demoted to military adjutant of Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 久乃除考功員外郎。

translations.literal: After a long while he was appointed Vice Director of Evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: Only after a long interval was he made Vice Director of Evaluations.

sentences.zh: 裴垍待之善，擢累給事中。

translations.literal: Pei Ji treated him well and promoted him through several posts to Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji treated him kindly and advanced him through several offices to Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 李吉甫當國而垍卒，不加贈，伯芻為申理，乃贈太子少傅。

translations.literal: When Li Jifu held sway and Ji died, no posthumous honors were granted; Bochu pleaded his case, and Ji was then made posthumous Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jifu was in power when Ji died without posthumous honors; Bochu argued on his behalf, and Ji was posthumously made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 或言其妻垍從母也，吉甫欲按之，求補虢州刺史。

translations.literal: Some said his wife was Ji's cousin on the mother's side; Jifu wished to investigate, and Bochu sought appointment as prefect of Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Some said his wife was Ji's cousin; Jifu wished to press the matter, and Bochu sought transfer as prefect of Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 稍遷刑部侍郎、左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Vice Minister of Justice and Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Minister of Justice and Left Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 伯芻風度高嚴，善談確，而動與時適，論者少之。

translations.literal: Bochu's bearing was lofty and stern; he was skilled at earnest discourse, yet his actions often suited the times, and critics held him in little esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Bochu bore himself with lofty severity and spoke with earnest conviction, yet he often trimmed his actions to the times, and critics thought little of him.

sentences.zh: 子 寬夫

translations.literal: Son Kuanfu
translations.idiomatic: His son Kuanfu

sentences.zh: 子寬夫，寶歷中為監察御史。

translations.literal: His son Kuanfu served as attendant censor during the Baoli reign.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kuanfu served as attendant censor during Baoli.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「以王府官攝祠，位輕，非嚴恭意，請以尚書省、東宮三品若左右丞、侍郎通攝。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Using princely household officials to preside at sacrifices is too light a station and not in the spirit of solemn reverence; I request that third-rank officials of the Department of State Affairs and the Eastern Palace, such as the Left and Right Vice Directors or vice ministers, preside in turn.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Having princely household officials preside at sacrifices is too low in rank and falls short of solemn reverence; let third-rank officials of the Secretariat and Eastern Palace, such as vice directors or vice ministers, preside instead."

sentences.zh: 」俄轉左補闕。

translations.literal: " Soon he was transferred to Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 陳岵註浮屠書，因供奉僧以聞，除濠州刺史。

translations.literal: Chen Hu annotated Buddhist texts and, through a resident monk, had word reach the throne; he was appointed prefect of Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hu annotated Buddhist texts and, through a resident monk at court, secured an appointment as prefect of Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 寬夫劾狀，敬宗怒謂宰相曰：「岵不繇僧得州，諫臣安受此言？

translations.literal: Kuanfu drafted an impeachment; Emperor Jingzong angrily told the chancellor: "Did Hu not obtain his prefecture through a monk? How can a remonstrance official accept such words?
translations.idiomatic: Kuanfu drafted an impeachment; Emperor Jingzong angrily told the chancellor: "Did Hu not win his prefecture through a monk? How can a remonstrance official speak this way?

sentences.zh: 」寬夫曰：「眾劾岵，獨臣草狀，應伏誅。

translations.literal: " Kuanfu said: "All impeached Hu; I alone drafted the memorial and deserve execution.
translations.idiomatic: Kuanfu replied: "All impeached Hu; I alone drafted the memorial and deserve death.

sentences.zh: 推言所從，恐累國體。

translations.literal: To trace who gave the words would, I fear, harm the dignity of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Tracing who gave such words would, I fear, harm the dignity of the state.

sentences.zh: 」帝讜其言，釋之。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved his words and released him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his point and pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 子 允章

translations.literal: Son Yunzhang
translations.idiomatic: His son Yunzhang

sentences.zh: 子允章，字蘊中，咸通中為禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Yunzhang, styled Yunzhong, served as Vice Minister of Rites during the Xiantong reign.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yunzhang, styled Yunzhong, served as Vice Minister of Rites during Xiantong.

sentences.zh: 請諸生及進士第並謁先師，衣青衿，介幘，以還古制。

translations.literal: He requested that students and jinshi degree-holders alike pay homage to the sage teacher, wearing blue collars and kerchiefs, to restore ancient practice.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that students and new jinshi alike pay homage to Confucius in blue collars and kerchiefs, restoring ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 改國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 又建言：「群臣輸光學錢治庠序，宰相五萬，節度使四萬，刺史萬。

translations.literal: He also proposed: "Let ministers contribute funds for the Directorate of Education to maintain the schools: chancellors fifty thousand, military governors forty thousand, prefects ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed that ministers contribute funds to maintain the schools: fifty thousand for chancellors, forty thousand for military governors, ten thousand for prefects.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: " The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 後為東都留守。

translations.literal: Later he served as military governor of the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as military governor of the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 黃巢至，分司李磎挈尚書印走河陽，允章寄治河清。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao arrived, Li Diao of the eastern-capital branch office took the seal of the Department of State Affairs and fled to Heyang; Yunzhang temporarily administered from Heqing.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao arrived, Li Diao of the eastern-capital branch took the Secretariat seal and fled to Heyang; Yunzhang governed temporarily from Heqing.

sentences.zh: 巢僭號，輒受偽官，文書盡用金統。

translations.literal: When Chao usurped a reign title, Yunzhang accepted a false appointment; all documents used the Jintong era name.
translations.idiomatic: When Chao declared himself emperor, Yunzhang accepted a rebel post; all documents used the Jintong reign title.

sentences.zh: 遣取印磎所，磎不與，更悔愧，移檄近鎮起兵扞賊，磎持印還之。

translations.literal: He sent men to take the seal from Diao's place; Diao would not yield it. Yunzhang then felt remorse, issued a proclamation to nearby commands to raise troops against the bandits, and Diao returned the seal.
translations.idiomatic: He sent men to seize the seal from Diao, who refused. Yunzhang then repented, called on nearby commands to raise troops against the rebels, and Diao returned the seal.

sentences.zh: 後廢於家。

translations.literal: Later he was dismissed and lived at home.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was dismissed and lived in retirement.

sentences.zh: 楊憑，字虛受，一字嗣仁，虢州弘農人。

translations.literal: Yang Ping, styled Xushou, also known as Siren, was a man of Hongnong in Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ping, whose style names were Xushou and Siren, came from Hongnong in Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 少孤，其母訓道有方。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, his mother instructed him with sound methods.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he was raised by a mother who taught him well.

sentences.zh: 長善文辭，與弟凝、淩皆有名。

translations.literal: When grown he excelled at literary composition; with his brothers Ning and Ling he was all celebrated.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he excelled at letters; he and his brothers Ning and Ling were all well known.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，踵擢進士第，時號「三楊」。

translations.literal: During the Dali reign they passed the jinshi examination in succession and were called at the time "the Three Yangs."
translations.idiomatic: During Dali they passed the jinshi in succession and were known as "the Three Yangs."

sentences.zh: 憑重交遊，尚氣節然諾，與穆質、許孟容、李庸阝相友善，一時歆慕，號「楊穆許李」。

translations.literal: Ping valued friendship, prized integrity and kept his word, and was intimate with Mu Zhi, Xu Mengrong, and Li Yong; men of the time admired them and called them "Yang, Mu, Xu, and Li."
translations.idiomatic: Ping prized friendship and honor, kept his promises, and was close to Mu Zhi, Xu Mengrong, and Li Yong; contemporaries admired them and called them "Yang, Mu, Xu, and Li."

sentences.zh: 歷事節度府，召為監察御史，不樂，輒免去。

translations.literal: He served in military headquarters, was summoned as attendant censor, disliked it, and promptly resigned.
translations.idiomatic: He served on military staffs, was summoned as attendant censor, disliked the post, and promptly resigned.

sentences.zh: 累遷太常少卿、湖南江西觀察使。

translations.literal: He was promoted through several posts to Vice Chamberlain of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and commissioner of the Hunan and Jiangxi circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Chamberlain of Sacrifices and commissioner of Hunan and Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 性簡傲，接下脫略，人多怨之。

translations.literal: His nature was blunt and proud; in dealing with subordinates he was careless, and many resented him.
translations.idiomatic: He was blunt and proud, careless with subordinates, and widely resented.

sentences.zh: 在二鎮尤侈忲。

translations.literal: In the two circuits he was especially extravagant and dissolute.
translations.idiomatic: In both circuits he was especially extravagant and dissolute.

sentences.zh: 入拜京兆尹。

translations.literal: He entered court and was appointed Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 與御史中丞李夷簡素有隙，因劾憑江西奸贓及它不法，詔刑部尚書李庸阝、大理卿趙昌即臺參訊。

translations.literal: He had long been at odds with Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Yijian, who impeached Ping for corruption in Jiangxi and other unlawful acts; an edict ordered Minister of Justice Li Yong and Chief Justice Zhao Chang to conduct immediate examination at the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He had long feuded with Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Yijian, who impeached him for corruption in Jiangxi and other crimes; the court ordered Minister of Justice Li Yong and Chief Justice Zhao Chang to interrogate him at the censorate at once.

sentences.zh: 於時憑治第永寧裏，功役叢煩，又幽妓妾於永樂別舍，謗議頗讙，故夷簡藉之痛擿發，欲抵以死。

translations.literal: At the time Ping was building a mansion in Yongning Lane with laborers thronging about, and he secluded singing girls and concubines in a separate lodge at Yongle; public censure was loud, so Yijian seized the chance to press hard and sought to have him punished with death.
translations.idiomatic: Ping was then building a mansion in Yongning Lane with labor in full cry and kept singing girls in a Yongle side lodge; scandal was loud, and Yijian seized the chance to press the case and sought his death.

sentences.zh: 既置對，未得狀，即逮捕故官屬推躡，簿憑家資。

translations.literal: After he was brought to face questioning, before a verdict was obtained his former subordinates were arrested and pressed, and his household assets were inventoried.
translations.idiomatic: After he was brought for questioning, before a verdict was reached his former subordinates were arrested and pressed, and his household assets were inventoried.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士李絳奏言：「憑所坐贓，不當同逆人法。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Li Jiang memorialized: "The corruption of which Ping stands accused should not be treated by the law for traitors.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Li Jiang memorialized: "Ping's corruption should not be punished under the law for traitors.

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " The proceedings then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The proceedings then ceased.

sentences.zh: 憲宗以憑治京兆有績，但貶臨賀尉。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong, noting Ping's achievements governing Jingzhao, demoted him only to sheriff of Linhe.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong, noting his record governing Jingzhao, demoted him only to sheriff of Linhe.

sentences.zh: 始，德宗時，假借方鎮，習為僭擬事，夷簡首按憑，時以為宜，而緣私怨，論者亦不與。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Dezong's time, military governors had borrowed power and grown accustomed to presumptuous acts; Yijian was the first to press a case against Ping, and men of the time thought it fitting, yet because it sprang from private resentment critics did not fully approve.
translations.idiomatic: Under Dezong, military governors had grown accustomed to presumptuous conduct; Yijian was the first to press a case against Ping, which many thought timely, yet because it sprang from private resentment critics withheld full approval.

sentences.zh: 俄徙杭州長史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Long Prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Long Prefect of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以太子詹事卒。

translations.literal: He died while serving as Chamberlain of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Chamberlain of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 憑所善客徐晦者，字大章，第進士、賢良方正，擢櫟陽尉。

translations.literal: Among Ping's favored clients was Xu Hui, styled Dazhang, who passed the jinshi and the erudite and upright examinations and was promoted to sheriff of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Among Ping's favored clients was Xu Hui, styled Dazhang, who passed the jinshi and erudite examinations and was made sheriff of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 憑得罪，姻友憚累，無往候者，獨晦至藍田慰餞。

translations.literal: When Ping fell into disgrace, relatives and friends feared entanglement and none came to see him off; Hui alone went to Lantian to console and bid him farewell.
translations.idiomatic: When Ping fell, kin and friends feared entanglement and none came to see him off; Hui alone went to Lantian to console and bid him farewell.

sentences.zh: 宰相權德輿謂曰：「君送臨賀誠厚，無乃為累乎？

translations.literal: Chancellor Quan Deyu said to him: "Your seeing off the man bound for Linhe is truly generous—will it not bring trouble upon you?
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Quan Deyu said: "Your farewell to the man bound for Linhe is generous—will it not bring trouble on you?

sentences.zh: 」晦曰：「方布衣時，臨賀知我，今忍遽棄邪？

translations.literal: " Hui said: "When I was still in plain cloth, the man now bound for Linhe knew me—how could I now bear to abandon him so suddenly?
translations.idiomatic: Hui replied: "When I was still unknown, the man now bound for Linhe knew me—how could I abandon him now?

sentences.zh: 有如公異時為奸邪譖斥，又可爾乎？

translations.literal: If someday you, sir, were slandered and driven out by wicked men, could one act otherwise?
translations.idiomatic: If someday you were slandered and driven out by wicked men, could one act otherwise?

sentences.zh: 」德輿嘆其直，稱之朝。

translations.literal: " Deyu sighed at his integrity and praised him at court.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu sighed at his integrity and praised him at court.

sentences.zh: 李夷簡遽表為監察御史，晦過謝，問所以舉之之由。

translations.literal: Li Yijian promptly memorialized to make him attendant censor; Hui came to thank him and asked the reason for the recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yijian promptly recommended him as attendant censor; Hui came to thank him and asked why he had been chosen.

sentences.zh: 夷簡曰：「君不負楊臨賀，肯負國乎？

translations.literal: Yijian said: "You did not fail Yang of Linhe—would you fail the state?
translations.idiomatic: Yijian said: "You did not fail Yang of Linhe—would you fail the state?"

sentences.zh: 」後歷中書舍人，強直守正，不沈浮於時。

translations.literal: " Later he served as Attendant of the Secretariat, firm and upright, not swaying with the times.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as Attendant of the Secretariat, firm and upright, unmoved by the currents of the age.

sentences.zh: 嗜酒喪明，以禮部尚書致仕，卒。

translations.literal: He loved wine and lost his sight, retired as Minister of Rites, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He drank heavily, lost his sight, retired as Minister of Rites, and died.

sentences.zh: 弟 凝

translations.literal: Younger brother Ning
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Ning

sentences.zh: 凝，字懋功。

translations.literal: Ning, styled Maogong.
translations.idiomatic: Ning, styled Maogong.

sentences.zh: 由協律郎三遷侍御史，為司封員外郎。

translations.literal: From Director of Harmonies he was thrice promoted to attendant censor and made Vice Director of Enfeoffments.
translations.idiomatic: From Director of Harmonies he rose thrice to attendant censor and became Vice Director of Enfeoffments.

sentences.zh: 坐厘正嫡媵封邑，為權幸所忌，徙吏部，稍遷右司郎中。

translations.literal: For rectifying the fiefs of principal wives and concubines he was resented by the powerful and favored, transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, and gradually promoted to Director of the Right Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: For rectifying the fiefs of principal wives and concubines he was resented by the powerful, transferred to Personnel, and rose to Director of the Right Bureau.

sentences.zh: 宣武董晉表為判官，亳州刺史缺，晉以凝行州事。

translations.literal: Dong Jin of Xuanwu memorialized to appoint him administrative aide; when the prefect of Bozhou was absent, Jin had Ning administer the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Jin of Xuanwu appointed him administrative aide; when Bozhou lacked a prefect, Jin had Ning administer the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 增墾田，決汙堰，築堤防，水患訖息。

translations.literal: He expanded reclaimed fields, opened silted weirs, and built dikes; flood troubles ceased altogether.
translations.idiomatic: He expanded reclaimed fields, cleared silted weirs, and built dikes until flooding ceased.

sentences.zh: 時孟叔度橫縱撓軍治，而凝亦荒湎，晉卒，亂作。

translations.literal: At the time Meng Shudu ran riot and obstructed military administration, while Ning also drank to excess; when Jin died, disorder broke out.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Shudu ran riot and obstructed military rule while Ning also drank heavily; when Jin died, mutiny broke out.

sentences.zh: 凝走還京師，闔門三年。

translations.literal: Ning fled back to the capital and kept his doors closed for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Ning fled to the capital and kept his doors closed for three years.

sentences.zh: 拜兵部郎中，以痼疾卒。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Ministry of War and died of a chronic illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Director of the Ministry of War and died of a chronic illness.

sentences.zh: 弟 淩

translations.literal: Younger brother Ling
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Ling

sentences.zh: 淩，字恭履，最善文，終侍御史。

translations.literal: Ling, styled Gonglu, was finest at letters and ended as attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: Ling, styled Gonglu, was finest at letters and ended as attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 子敬之。

translations.literal: His son was Jingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Jingzhi.

sentences.zh: 淩子 敬之

translations.literal: Ling's son Jingzhi
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhi, son of Ling

sentences.zh: 敬之，字茂孝。

translations.literal: Jingzhi, styled Maoxiao.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhi, styled Maoxiao.

sentences.zh: 元和初，擢進士第，平判入等，遷右衛胄曹參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he passed the jinshi, entered the top rank in the parallel judgment, and was appointed Army Aide of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanhe he passed the jinshi, ranked at the top in the parallel judgment, and was made Army Aide of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 累遷屯田、戶部二郎中。

translations.literal: He was promoted through several posts to Second Director of the Granary and Revenue bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Second Director of the Granary and Revenue bureaus.

sentences.zh: 坐李宗閔黨，貶連州刺史。

translations.literal: For association with Li Zongmin's faction he was demoted to prefect of Lianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For ties to Li Zongmin's faction he was demoted to prefect of Lianzhou.

sentences.zh: 文宗尚儒術，以宰相鄭覃兼國子祭酒，俄以敬之代。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong valued Confucian learning and made Chancellor Zheng Tan concurrently Chancellor of the Directorate of Education; soon Jingzhi replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong valued Confucian learning and made Chancellor Zheng Tan concurrently Chancellor of the Directorate of Education; soon Jingzhi replaced him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，兼太常少卿。

translations.literal: Before long he also held the post of Vice Chamberlain of Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he also served as Vice Chamberlain of Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 是日，二子戎、戴登科，時號「楊家三喜」。

translations.literal: That day his two sons Rong and Dai passed the examinations; men of the time called it "three joys for the Yang family."
translations.idiomatic: That day his sons Rong and Dai passed the examinations; contemporaries called it "three joys for the Yang family."

sentences.zh: 轉大理卿，檢校工部尚書，兼祭酒，卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Justice, made acting Minister of Works with concurrent duty as Chancellor of Education, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He became Chief Justice, acting Minister of Works with concurrent duty as Chancellor of Education, and died.

sentences.zh: 敬之嘗為《華山賦》示韓愈，愈稱之，士林一時傳布，李德裕尤咨賞。

translations.literal: Jingzhi once composed a "Mount Hua Rhapsody" and showed it to Han Yu; Han praised it, and the scholarly world spread it at once; Li Deyu especially admired it.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhi once wrote a "Mount Hua Rhapsody" and showed it to Han Yu, who praised it; scholars spread it at once, and Li Deyu especially admired it.

sentences.zh: 敬之愛士類，得其文章，孜孜玩諷，人以為癖。

translations.literal: Jingzhi loved men of letters; whenever he obtained their writings he studied and recited them tirelessly—people regarded it as an obsession.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhi loved men of letters; whenever he obtained their writings he studied them tirelessly, and people thought it an obsession.

sentences.zh: 雅愛項斯為詩，所至稱之，繇是擢上第。

translations.literal: He especially admired Xiang Si's poetry and praised it wherever he went; thereby Si was placed at the top of the examination list.
translations.idiomatic: He especially admired Xiang Si's poetry and praised it wherever he went, and thereby Si won the top rank on the examination.

sentences.zh: 斯，字子遷，江東人。

translations.literal: Si, styled Ziqian, was a man of Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Si, styled Ziqian, came from Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 敬之祖客灞上，見閩人濮陽願，閱其文，大推挹，遍語公卿間。

translations.literal: Jingzhi's grandfather was a guest at Ba Shang and met Pu Yangyuan of Fujian; reading his writings, he greatly commended them and spoke of them among all the high ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhi's grandfather was lodging at Ba Shang when he met Pu Yangyuan of Fujian, read his writings, greatly commended them, and spoke of him among the high ministers.

sentences.zh: 會願死，敬之為斂葬。

translations.literal: When Yuan died, Jingzhi arranged his burial.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan died, Jingzhi arranged his burial.

sentences.zh: 潘孟陽

translations.literal: Pan Mengyang
translations.idiomatic: Pan Mengyang

sentences.zh: 潘孟陽，史亡何所人。

translations.literal: Pan Mengyang—the history does not record where he was from.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Mengyang—the history does not record his birthplace.

sentences.zh: 父炎，大歷末官右庶子，為元載所惡，久不遷。

translations.literal: His father Yan, at the end of Dali held the post of Right Vice Counselor of the Heir Apparent; he was disliked by Yuan Zai and long went without promotion.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan, late in Dali, was Right Vice Counselor of the Heir Apparent; Yuan Zai disliked him and he long went without promotion.

sentences.zh: 載誅，進禮部侍郎，以病免。

translations.literal: When Zai was executed, Yan was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and retired on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Zai was executed, Yan was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 方劉晏任權，炎乃其婿，雖書疏報答，未嘗輒開，時稱有古人節。

translations.literal: When Liu Yan held power, Yan was his son-in-law; though they exchanged letters, Yan never opened them lightly, and men of the time praised his ancient integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yan held power, Yan was his son-in-law; though they exchanged letters, Yan never opened them lightly, and contemporaries praised his old-fashioned integrity.

sentences.zh: 晏得罪，坐貶澧州司馬，時輿疾上道，不自言。

translations.literal: When Yan fell into disgrace he was punished and demoted to Sima of Lizhou; at the time he was ill in his carriage on the road and did not speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan fell, he was demoted to Sima of Lizhou; ill in his carriage on the road, he did not speak of his suffering.

sentences.zh: 於邵高其介，申救，不見聽。

translations.literal: Yu Shao admired his integrity and pleaded for him, but the plea was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shao admired his integrity and pleaded for him, but the plea was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 孟陽少以蔭，俄登博學宏辭科，補渭南尉，再遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Mengyang entered office young by yin privilege, soon passed the erudite and eloquent examination, was appointed sheriff of Weinan, and was twice promoted to palace attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: Mengyang entered office young by yin privilege, soon passed the erudite examination, was made sheriff of Weinan, and twice rose to palace attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 公卿多父行及外家賓客，故被慰薦，擢累兵部郎中。

translations.literal: Many high ministers were his father's peers or his maternal family's guests, so he received consolation and recommendation and was promoted through several posts to Director of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Many high ministers were his father's peers or maternal kin, so he received recommendation and rose to Director of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 貞元末，王紹以恩幸進，數稱孟陽才，權知戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenyuan, Wang Shao advanced through imperial favor and repeatedly praised Mengyang's talent; he was given acting charge as Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Zhenyuan, Wang Shao advanced through imperial favor and repeatedly praised Mengyang's talent; he was given acting charge as Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 杜佑判度支，奏以自副。

translations.literal: Du You, who oversaw the treasury, memorialized to make him his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Du You, who oversaw the treasury, memorialized to make him his deputy.

sentences.zh: 時憲宗新立，詔孟陽馳驛江淮視財賦，加鹽鐵轉運副使，並察諸使治否。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong had newly acceded, an edict ordered Mengyang to travel post-haste through Jiang and Huai to inspect revenues and taxes, with the additional post of deputy salt-and-iron transport commissioner, and also to examine whether the various commissioners governed well or ill.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong had newly acceded, an edict ordered Mengyang to travel post-haste through Jiang and Huai to inspect revenues, with the additional post of deputy salt-and-iron transport commissioner and authority to examine the conduct of commissioners.

sentences.zh: 孟陽恃奧主，又氣豪倨，從者數百人，所至會賓客，留連倡樂，招金錢，多補吏，譽望大喪。

translations.literal: Mengyang relied on his powerful patron, was moreover proud and overbearing, and had several hundred followers; wherever he went he gathered guests, lingered with singers and musicians, solicited money, and appointed many subordinates—the reputation he had enjoyed was largely lost.
translations.idiomatic: Mengyang relied on his powerful patron and was proud and overbearing; with several hundred followers he entertained guests everywhere, lingered with singers, solicited money, and appointed many subordinates, and his reputation collapsed.

sentences.zh: 使還，罷為大理卿。

translations.literal: When his mission returned, he was removed and made Chief Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned from his mission, he was removed and made Chief Justice.

sentences.zh: 其後左司郎中鄭敬宣慰江淮，帝誡曰：「朕宮中用尺寸物皆有籍，唯賑民無所計。

translations.literal: Later Left Bureau Director Zheng Jing was sent to console Jiang and Huai; the emperor admonished him: "In my palace even items measured by the inch are all recorded; only relief for the people has no limit.
translations.idiomatic: Later Left Bureau Director Zheng Jing was sent to console Jiang and Huai; the emperor warned him: "In my palace even items measured by the inch are all recorded; only relief for the people has no limit.

sentences.zh: 卿是行，宜諭朕意，毋若潘孟陽殫財費酣飲遊山寺而已。」

translations.literal: On this mission you should convey my intent—do not, like Pan Mengyang, exhaust funds in drinking and visiting mountain temples alone."
translations.idiomatic: On this mission convey my intent—do not, like Pan Mengyang, exhaust funds in drinking and visiting mountain temples alone."

sentences.zh: 元和三年，出為華州刺史，遷劍南東川節度使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanhe he was sent out as prefect of Huazhou and transferred to military governor of the Jiannan East circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanhe he was sent out as prefect of Huazhou and made military governor of the Jiannan East circuit.

sentences.zh: 宰相武元衡與孟陽舊，復以戶部侍郎召判度支，又兼京北五城營田使。

translations.literal: Chancellor Wu Yuanheng was old friends with Mengyang and recalled him as Vice Minister of Revenue to oversee the treasury, with the additional post of commissioner for the five northern cities' military farms.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Wu Yuanheng, an old friend of Mengyang, recalled him as Vice Minister of Revenue to oversee the treasury, with the additional post of commissioner for the five northern cities' military farms.

sentences.zh: 太府王遂為西北供軍使，持營田不可，至私忿恨，更請間論列。

translations.literal: Wang Sui of the Court of the Imperial Treasury served as supply commissioner for the northwest armies and opposed the military farms; private resentment grew until he repeatedly requested a separate audience to argue the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sui of the Imperial Treasury served as northwest supply commissioner and opposed the military farms; resentment grew until he repeatedly requested a separate audience to argue the case.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，罷孟陽左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and removed Mengyang to Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and demoted Mengyang to Left Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 明年，復舊官。

translations.literal: The next year he was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was restored to his former office.

sentences.zh: 盛葺第舍，帝微行至樂遊原，望見之，以問左右，孟陽懼，輟不敢治。

translations.literal: He lavishly repaired his residence; the emperor made an informal visit to Leyou Plateau, saw it in the distance, and asked his attendants. Mengyang grew fearful and stopped the work.
translations.idiomatic: He lavishly repaired his residence; the emperor made an informal visit to Leyou Plateau, saw it in the distance, and asked his attendants. Mengyang grew fearful and halted the work.

sentences.zh: 而伎媵用度過侈汰，人多指怒之。

translations.literal: Yet his spending on performers and concubines was excessively wasteful, and many pointed to him in anger.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his spending on performers and concubines was wasteful in the extreme, and many denounced him.

sentences.zh: 病風痹，復改左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He fell ill with wind paralysis and was again transferred to Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill with wind paralysis and was again made Left Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈兵部尚書，謚曰康。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Minister of War, with the posthumous title Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Minister of War, with the posthumous epithet Kang.

sentences.zh: 初，孟陽為侍郎，年未四十，其母謂曰：「以爾之材而位丞郎，使吾憂之。」

translations.literal: At the outset, when Mengyang was vice minister and not yet forty, his mother said: "With your talent to hold a vice minister's post makes me anxious."
translations.idiomatic: Early on, when Mengyang was vice minister and not yet forty, his mother said: "With your talent to hold a vice minister's post at your age fills me with worry."

sentences.zh: 崔元略

translations.literal: Cui Yuanlue
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuanlue

sentences.zh: 崔元略，博州人。

translations.literal: Cui Yuanlue was a man of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuanlue came from Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 父敬，貞元時終尚書左丞。

translations.literal: His father Jing served to the end of the Zhenyuan period as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jing ended his career in Zhenyuan as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 元略第進士，更辟諸府，遷累殿中侍御史，以刑部郎中知御史雜事，進拜中丞。

translations.literal: Yuanlue passed the jinshi, served in succession in various headquarters, was promoted through several posts to palace attendant censor, handled miscellaneous censorate affairs as Director of the Ministry of Justice, and was advanced to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlue passed the jinshi, served in various headquarters, rose to palace attendant censor, handled miscellaneous censorate affairs as Director of Justice, and was made Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 時李夷簡召為大夫，故詔元略留司東臺。

translations.literal: At the time Li Yijian was summoned as Censor-in-Chief, so an edict ordered Yuanlue to remain at the eastern-capital branch office.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yijian was then summoned as Censor-in-Chief, so Yuanlue was ordered to remain at the eastern-capital branch office.

sentences.zh: 改京兆少尹，行府事，數月，遷為尹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Junior Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, administered the prefecture for several months, and was then promoted to governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Junior Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, administered the prefecture for several months, and was then promoted to governor.

sentences.zh: 徙左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Left Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 初，中丞缺，議者屬崔植，而元略謬謂植入閣不如儀，使御史彈治。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the vice censor-in-chief post was vacant, critics expected Cui Zhi, but Yuanlue falsely said Zhi had entered the inner court without proper ceremony and had censors impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: When the vice censor-in-chief post was vacant, critics expected Cui Zhi, but Yuanlue falsely claimed Zhi had entered the inner court without proper ceremony and had censors impeach him.

sentences.zh: 及宰相以二人進，元略果得之，植恨悵。

translations.literal: When the chancellor presented two candidates, Yuanlue indeed obtained the post; Zhi was resentful and dejected.
translations.idiomatic: When the chancellor presented two candidates, Yuanlue won the post; Zhi was resentful and dejected.

sentences.zh: 既當國，以元略為宣撫党項使，辭疾不行。

translations.literal: Once Zhi held power, he appointed Yuanlue commissioner to console the Tangut tribes, but Yuanlue pleaded illness and would not go.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhi held power, he appointed Yuanlue commissioner to console the Tangut tribes; Yuanlue pleaded illness and refused to go.

sentences.zh: 植奏：「不少責，無以示群臣。

translations.literal: Zhi memorialized: "If he is not punished at all, there is no way to show the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi memorialized: "If he is not punished at all, there is no way to show the ministers.

sentences.zh: 」乃出為黔南觀察使，徙鄂嶽。

translations.literal: " He was then sent out as commissioner of Qiannan and transferred to E-Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as commissioner of Qiannan and transferred to E-Yue.

sentences.zh: 久乃拜大理卿。

translations.literal: After a long while he was appointed Chief Justice.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was made Chief Justice.

sentences.zh: 敬宗初，還京兆尹，兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingzong's reign he returned as Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao with the additional title of Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingzong's reign he returned as Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao with the additional title of Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 收貸錢萬七千緡，為御史劾奏，詔刑部郎中趙元亮、大理正元從質、侍御史溫造以三司雜治。

translations.literal: He collected loan money of seventeen thousand strings of cash and was impeached by censors; an edict ordered Director of Justice Zhao Yuanliang, Senior Justice Yuan Congzhi, and Vice Censor Wen Zao to conduct joint investigation by the three bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: He collected loan money of seventeen thousand strings and was impeached; the court ordered Zhao Yuanliang of Justice, Yuan Congzhi of the Court of Review, and Vice Censor Wen Zao to conduct a joint investigation.

sentences.zh: 元略素事宦人崔潭峻，頗左右之，獄具，削兼秩而已。

translations.literal: Yuanlue had long served the eunuch Cui Tanjun and was much influenced by him; when the case was concluded, only his concurrent rank was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlue had long served the eunuch Cui Tanjun and was much influenced by him; when the case concluded, only his concurrent rank was stripped.

sentences.zh: 俄授戶部侍郎，譏謗大興，諫官斥元略方劾而遷，有助力，元略自解辨，乃止。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue; ridicule arose on a large scale, and remonstrance officials denounced Yuanlue for being promoted right after impeachment with help behind the scenes; Yuanlue defended himself and the matter ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Vice Minister of Revenue; ridicule arose widely, and remonstrance officials denounced his promotion right after impeachment as backed by hidden influence; Yuanlue defended himself and the matter died down.

sentences.zh: 京兆劉棲楚又劾元略前造東渭橋，縱吏增估物不償直，取工徒贓二萬緡。

translations.literal: Liu Qichu of Jingzhao again impeached Yuanlue for earlier building the East Wei Bridge, allowing clerks to inflate estimates and not pay fair value, and taking bribes from laborers of twenty thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qichu of Jingzhao again impeached Yuanlue for building the East Wei Bridge, allowing clerks to inflate estimates without paying fair value and taking twenty thousand strings in bribes from laborers.

sentences.zh: 詔奪一月俸。

translations.literal: An edict stripped one month's salary.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped one month's salary.

sentences.zh: 於是棲楚規相位，疑元略妨己路，故舉疑似蔑染之。

translations.literal: Qichu then aimed at the chancellorship and suspected Yuanlue blocked his path, so he raised doubtful charges to smear him.
translations.idiomatic: Qichu then aimed at the chancellorship and suspected Yuanlue blocked his path, so he raised doubtful charges to smear him.

sentences.zh: 太和三年，以戶部尚書判度支，出為東都留守，改義成節度使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taihe he was made Minister of Revenue overseeing the treasury, sent out as military governor of the eastern capital, and transferred to military governor of Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taihe he was made Minister of Revenue overseeing the treasury, sent out as military governor of the eastern capital, and transferred to military governor of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 子鉉。

translations.literal: His son was Xian.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Xian.

sentences.zh: 子 鉉

translations.literal: Son Xian
translations.idiomatic: His son Xian

sentences.zh: 鉉，字臺碩，擢進士第，從李石荊南為賓佐，入拜司勛員外郎、翰林學士，遷中書舍人、學士承旨。

translations.literal: Xian, styled Taishuo, passed the jinshi, followed Li Shi to Jingnan as a staff member, entered court as Vice Director of Merits and Hanlin Academician, and was promoted to Attendant of the Secretariat and Chief Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Xian, styled Taishuo, passed the jinshi, served Li Shi in Jingnan as a staff member, entered court as Vice Director of Merits and Hanlin Academician, and rose to Attendant of the Secretariat and Chief Academician.

sentences.zh: 武宗好蹴踘、角抵，鉉切諫，帝褒納之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong loved cuju and wrestling; Xian remonstrated sharply, and the emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong loved cuju and wrestling; Xian remonstrated sharply, and the emperor praised and accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 會昌三年，拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huichang he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Huichang he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 鉉入朝，凡三歲至宰相，而石猶在江陵。

translations.literal: From Xian's entry at court, in only three years he reached the chancellorship, while Shi was still at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: From his entry at court, Xian reached the chancellorship in only three years while Shi was still at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 澤潞平，兼戶部尚書。

translations.literal: When Ze-Lu was pacified, he was given the additional post of Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Ze-Lu was pacified, he was given the additional post of Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 與李德裕不叶，罷為陜虢觀察使。

translations.literal: He was at odds with Li Deyu and was removed to commissioner of Shan-Guo.
translations.idiomatic: He fell out with Li Deyu and was removed to commissioner of Shan-Guo.

sentences.zh: 宣宗初，擢河中節度使，以御史大夫召，用會昌故官輔政，進尚書左僕射，兼門下侍郎，封博陵郡公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuanzong's reign he was promoted to military governor of Hezhong, summoned as Censor-in-Chief, employed former Huichang officials to assist in government, advanced to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs with concurrent duty as Vice Director of the Chancellery, and enfeoffed as Duke of Boling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xuanzong's reign he was promoted to military governor of Hezhong, recalled as Censor-in-Chief, employed former Huichang officials to assist in government, advanced to Left Vice Director with concurrent duty as Vice Director of the Chancellery, and enfeoffed as Duke of Boling.

sentences.zh: 鉉所善者鄭魯、楊紹復、段瑰、薛蒙，頗參議論。

translations.literal: Those Xian favored were Zheng Lu, Yang Shaofu, Duan Gui, and Xue Meng, who often joined in deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Those Xian favored were Zheng Lu, Yang Shaofu, Duan Gui, and Xue Meng, who often joined in policy deliberation.

sentences.zh: 時語曰：「鄭、楊、段、薛，炙手可熱；

translations.literal: A saying of the time ran: "Zheng, Yang, Duan, and Xue—scorching to the touch;
translations.idiomatic: A saying of the time ran: "Zheng, Yang, Duan, and Xue—too hot to touch;

sentences.zh: 欲得命通，魯、紹、瑰、蒙。

translations.literal: to obtain an appointment, Lu, Shao, Gui, and Meng."
translations.idiomatic: to win an appointment, Lu, Shao, Gui, and Meng."

sentences.zh: 」帝聞之，題於扆。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard it, he wrote it on the screen behind his throne.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard it, he wrote it on the screen behind his throne.

sentences.zh: 是時，魯為刑部侍郎，鉉欲引以相，帝不許，用為河南尹。

translations.literal: At the time Lu was Vice Minister of Justice; Xian wished to bring him in as chancellor, but the emperor did not permit it and appointed him Metropolitan Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Lu was then Vice Minister of Justice; Xian wished to make him chancellor, but the emperor refused and appointed him Metropolitan Governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 它日，帝語鉉曰：「魯去矣，事由卿否？

translations.literal: Another day the emperor said to Xian: "Lu is gone—was it because of you?
translations.idiomatic: Another day the emperor said to Xian: "Lu is gone—was that your doing?

sentences.zh: 」鉉惶懼謝罪。

translations.literal: " Xian was fearful and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was fearful and apologized.

sentences.zh: 久之，出為淮南節度使，帝餞太液亭，賜詩寵之。

translations.literal: After a long while he was sent out as military governor of Huainan; the emperor feasted him at Taiye Pavilion and bestowed a poem in favor.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was sent out as military governor of Huainan; the emperor feasted him at Taiye Pavilion and bestowed a poem in honor.

sentences.zh: 因宣州軍亂，逐觀察使鄭薰，鉉出兵討擊，詔兼宣歙池觀察使。

translations.literal: When the Xuanzhou army mutinied and drove out Commissioner Zheng Xun, Xian sent troops to attack; an edict made him concurrently commissioner of Xuan, She, and Chi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xuanzhou army mutinied and drove out Commissioner Zheng Xun, Xian sent troops to suppress them and was made concurrently commissioner of Xuan, She, and Chi.

sentences.zh: 既平，加檢校司空，罷兼使。

translations.literal: After pacification he was given the acting title of Minister of Works and relieved of the concurrent commission.
translations.idiomatic: After pacification he was given the acting title of Minister of Works and relieved of the concurrent commission.

sentences.zh: 居九年，條教一下無復改，民以順賴。

translations.literal: He dwelt there nine years; once regulations were issued they were never changed again, and the people relied on him in obedience.
translations.idiomatic: He governed there nine years; once regulations were issued they were never changed, and the people relied on him in obedience.

sentences.zh: 咸通初，徙山南東道、荊南二鎮，封魏國公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiantong he was transferred to the Shanxi East and Jingnan circuits and enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiantong he was transferred to the Shanxi East and Jingnan circuits and enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 龐勛叛，自桂管北還，所過剽略。

translations.literal: Pang Xun rebelled and returned north from Guiguan, plundering wherever he passed.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xun rebelled and returned north from Guiguan, plundering wherever he passed.

sentences.zh: 鉉聞，大募兵屯江、湘，邀賊歸路。

translations.literal: When Xian heard of it, he raised troops on a large scale and stationed them on the Jiang and Xiang to block the bandits' return route.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of it, Xian raised a large force and stationed troops on the Jiang and Xiang to block the rebels' return route.

sentences.zh: 賊懼，更逾嶺，自淮而北。

translations.literal: The bandits grew fearful, crossed the ranges again, and went north from the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels grew fearful, crossed the ranges again, and marched north from the Huai.

sentences.zh: 朝廷壯其忠。

translations.literal: The court admired his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The court admired his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 卒官下。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 子 沆

translations.literal: Son Hang
translations.idiomatic: His son Hang

sentences.zh: 子沆，字內融，累遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: His son Hang, styled Neirong, was promoted through several posts to Attendant of the Secretariat.
