translations.idiomatic: His son Hang, styled Neirong, rose to Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 韋保衡逐於琮，沆亦貶循州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: When Wei Baoheng drove out Yu Cong, Hang was also demoted to revenue adjutant of Xunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Baoheng drove out Yu Cong, Hang was also demoted to revenue adjutant of Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 僖宗立，召為永州刺史，復拜舍人，進禮部、吏部二侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong acceded, Hang was summoned as prefect of Yongzhou, again appointed Attendant, and advanced to Vice Minister of Rites and Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong acceded, Hang was recalled as prefect of Yongzhou, again made Attendant, and advanced to Vice Minister of Rites and Personnel.

sentences.zh: 乾符五年，以戶部侍郎同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qianfu he was made Vice Minister of Revenue and Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Qianfu he was made Vice Minister of Revenue and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 昕旦告麻，大霧塞廷中，百僚就班修慶，大風雨雹，時謂不祥。

translations.literal: At dawn when the hemp edict was announced, heavy fog filled the court; when the hundred officials took their places for congratulation, a great wind with rain and hail arose—men of the time called it inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn when the hemp edict was announced, heavy fog filled the court; as officials took their places to congratulate, a great wind with rain and hail arose—men of the time called it inauspicious.

sentences.zh: 俄改中書侍郎，兼工部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat with concurrent duty as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat with concurrent duty as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 時王景崇進兼中書令，讓其兄景儒，求易定節度。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Jingchong was advanced to concurrent Grand Mentor of the Secretariat and yielded the post to his elder brother Jingru, seeking the Yiding military governorship.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingchong was then advanced to concurrent Grand Mentor and yielded the post to his elder brother Jingru, seeking the Yiding military governorship.

sentences.zh: 沆謂魏博、盧龍且相援，執不可。

translations.literal: Hang said Weibo and Lulong would support each other and firmly opposed it.
translations.idiomatic: Hang said Weibo and Lulong would support each other and firmly opposed it.

sentences.zh: 盧攜專政，而黃巢勢浸盛，沆每建裁遏，多為攜沮抑。

translations.literal: Lu Xie monopolized government while Huang Chao's power grew daily; Hang often proposed measures to restrain him, but most were blocked by Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xie monopolized government while Huang Chao's power grew daily; Hang often proposed measures to restrain him, but Xie blocked most of them.

sentences.zh: 賊陷京師，匿張直方第，遇害。

translations.literal: When the bandits took the capital, he hid in Zhang Zhifang's residence and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels took the capital, he hid in Zhang Zhifang's residence and was killed.

sentences.zh: 元略弟元受、元式、元儒，皆舉進士第。

translations.literal: Yuanlue's younger brothers Yuanshou, Yuanshi, and Yuanru all passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlue's younger brothers Yuanshou, Yuanshi, and Yuanru all passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 弟 元受

translations.literal: Younger brother Yuanshou
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yuanshou

sentences.zh: 元受以高陵尉直史館。

translations.literal: Yuanshou served as sheriff of Gaoling with duty at the Historiography Office.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshou served as sheriff of Gaoling with duty at the Historiography Office.

sentences.zh: 元和時，於臯謨為河北行營糧料使，元受從之，督供饋。

translations.literal: During Yuanhe, Yu Gaomo was supply commissioner for the Hebei campaign headquarters; Yuanshou followed him and supervised provisions.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanhe, Yu Gaomo was supply commissioner for the Hebei campaign; Yuanshou followed him and supervised provisions.

sentences.zh: 臯謨得罪，元受逐死嶺表。

translations.literal: When Gaomo fell into disgrace, Yuanshou was driven to die in the Lingnan frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaomo fell, Yuanshou was driven to his death in the Lingnan frontier.

sentences.zh: 弟 元式

translations.literal: Younger brother Yuanshi
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yuanshi

sentences.zh: 元式始署帥府僚佐，累官湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: Yuanshi first served on a military governor's staff and rose through several posts to commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshi first served on a military governor's staff and rose to commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 會昌中，澤潞用兵，遷河中，拜河東、義成節度使。

translations.literal: During Huichang, when Ze-Lu was at war, he was transferred to Hezhong and appointed military governor of Hedong and Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: During Huichang, when Ze-Lu was at war, he was transferred to Hezhong and made military governor of Hedong and Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 宣宗初，以刑部尚書判度支，拜門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事，進兼戶部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuanzong's reign he was made Minister of Justice overseeing the treasury, appointed Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Councilor, and advanced to concurrent Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xuanzong's reign he was made Minister of Justice overseeing the treasury, Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Councilor, and advanced to concurrent Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 以疾罷。

translations.literal: He retired on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司空，謚曰莊。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Minister of Works, with the posthumous title Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Works, with the posthumous epithet Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 大中時，又有宰相崔龜從，字玄告。

translations.literal: During the Dazhong period there was also Chancellor Cui Guicong, styled Xuangao.
translations.idiomatic: During Dazhong there was also Chancellor Cui Guicong, styled Xuangao.

sentences.zh: 初舉進士，復以賢良方正、拔萃，三中其科，拜右拾遺。

translations.literal: He first passed the jinshi, then passed the erudite and upright and the extraordinary selection examinations, winning top rank in all three, and was appointed Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: He first passed the jinshi, then passed the erudite and upright and extraordinary selection examinations, winning top rank in all three, and was made Right Reminder.

sentences.zh: 太和初，遷太常博士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe he was transferred to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taihe he was made Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 最明禮家沿革，問不虛酬。

translations.literal: He was most versed in the evolution of ritual practice and never answered a question without substance.
translations.idiomatic: He was most versed in the evolution of ritual practice and never answered a question without substance.

sentences.zh: 定敬宗廟室祝辭，皇帝不可雲孝弟。

translations.literal: He fixed the prayer texts for Emperor Jingzong's temple chambers: the emperor could not speak of filial piety and brotherly duty.
translations.idiomatic: He fixed the prayer texts for Emperor Jingzong's temple chambers: the emperor could not speak of filial piety and brotherly duty.

sentences.zh: 九宮皆列星，不容為大祠。

translations.literal: The Nine Palaces were all listed stars and could not be treated as major sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The Nine Palaces were all listed stars and could not be treated as major sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 大臣薨，不於訃日輟朝，乃在數日外。

translations.literal: When a great minister died, court was not suspended on the day of the death announcement but several days later.
translations.idiomatic: When a great minister died, court was not suspended on the day of the death announcement but several days later.

sentences.zh: 因引貞觀時，任瑰卒，有司對仗奏，太宗責其不知禮；

translations.literal: He cited the Zhenguan period: when Ren Gui died, the relevant office reported facing the imperial guard, and Taizong reproached them for not knowing ritual;
translations.idiomatic: He cited Zhenguan: when Ren Gui died, the relevant office reported facing the imperial guard, and Taizong reproached them for not knowing ritual;

sentences.zh: 岑文本歿，是夕罷警嚴；

translations.literal: when Cen Wende died, that very evening the night watch was suspended;
translations.idiomatic: when Cen Wende died, that very evening the night watch was suspended;

sentences.zh: 張公謹亡，哭不避辰日；

translations.literal: when Zhang Gongjin died, mourning did not avoid taboo days;
translations.idiomatic: when Zhang Gongjin died, mourning did not avoid taboo days;

sentences.zh: 故閔悼之切，不宜過時。

translations.literal: therefore heartfelt mourning should not be delayed.
translations.idiomatic: therefore heartfelt mourning should not be delayed.

sentences.zh: 又言三品以上官，非經任將相密近，不宜輟朝。

translations.literal: He also said that officials of third rank and above who had not served as generals, chancellors, or close attendants should not warrant suspension of court.
translations.idiomatic: He also said that officials of third rank and above who had not served as generals, chancellors, or close attendants should not warrant suspension of court.

sentences.zh: 詔皆可其議，九宮遂為中祠。

translations.literal: Edicts approved all his proposals, and the Nine Palaces were henceforth treated as middle sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts approved all his proposals, and the Nine Palaces were henceforth treated as middle sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 再遷至司勛郎中，知制誥，真拜中書舍人，歷戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was twice promoted to Director of Merits, drafted edicts, was formally appointed Attendant of the Secretariat, and served as Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Director of Merits, drafted edicts, was formally made Attendant of the Secretariat, and served as Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 大中四年，以中書侍郎同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dazhong he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Dazhong he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 再歲，罷為宣武軍節度使，數徙鎮，卒。

translations.literal: After two years he was removed to military governor of the Xuanwu army, transferred through several commands, and died.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he was removed to military governor of the Xuanwu army, transferred through several commands, and died.

sentences.zh: 韋綬，字子章，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Wei Shou, styled Zizhang, was a man of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou, whose style name was Zizhang, came from Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 有至性，然好不經，喪父，镵臂血寫浮屠書。

translations.literal: He had utmost filial nature, yet his pursuits were unorthodox; when his father died, he carved his arm and wrote Buddhist texts in blood.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply filial, yet his pursuits were unorthodox; when his father died, he carved his arm and wrote Buddhist texts in blood.

sentences.zh: 建中末，為長安尉。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jianzhong era he served as sheriff of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Jianzhong era he served as sheriff of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 朱泚亂，羸服走奉天，拜華陰令。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci rebelled, he fled to Fengtian in worn garments and was appointed magistrate of Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rebelled, he fled to Fengtian in ragged clothes and was made magistrate of Huayin.

sentences.zh: 佐襄陽於頔府，數譏謔刺頔橫恣，頔不能容，薦諸朝。

translations.literal: He assisted at Xiangyang on Yu Di's staff, repeatedly mocking and satirizing Di's lawless arrogance; Di could not tolerate him and recommended him to the court.
translations.idiomatic: He served at Xiangyang on Yu Di's staff, repeatedly mocking Di's lawless arrogance; Di could not tolerate him and recommended him to court.

sentences.zh: 三遷職方郎中。

translations.literal: He was thrice promoted to Director of the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He was thrice promoted to Director of the Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 穆宗為太子，綬入侍讀，遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When Muzong was heir apparent, Shou entered to serve as reader-in-waiting and was promoted to Remonstrance Official.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong was heir apparent, Shou served as reader-in-waiting and was promoted to Remonstrance Official.

sentences.zh: 太子書「依」字輒去「人」，曰：「上以此可天下事，烏得全書耶？

translations.literal: When the heir wrote the character "rely" he would omit the "person" radical and say: "The sovereign uses this to handle the affairs of the realm—how can one write it whole?
translations.idiomatic: When the heir wrote the character for "rely" he omitted the "person" radical and said: "The sovereign uses this to handle the realm's affairs—how can one write it whole?

sentences.zh: 」綬白之，帝喜，即賜綬錦彩。

translations.literal: " Shou reported this; the emperor was pleased and at once bestowed brocade on Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Shou reported this; the emperor was pleased and at once bestowed brocade on him.

sentences.zh: 方太子幼，綬數為俚言以悅太子，它日侍，太子為帝道之。

translations.literal: While the heir was still young, Shou often used vulgar speech to please him; another day while attending, the heir told the emperor about it.
translations.idiomatic: While the heir was still young, Shou often used vulgar speech to please him; one day while attending, the heir told the emperor about it.

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「綬當以經義輔導太子，而反語此，朕何賴焉？

translations.literal: The emperor angrily said: "Shou ought to guide the heir with classical principles, yet instead speaks thus—what can I rely on?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor angrily said: "Shou ought to guide the heir with classical principles, yet instead speaks thus—what can I rely on?

sentences.zh: 」外遷虔州刺史。

translations.literal: " He was sent out as prefect of Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，召為尚書右丞、集賢院學士，出入禁中，怙寵甚。

translations.literal: When Muzong acceded, Shou was summoned as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Academician of the Hall of Assembled Eminences, entering and leaving the inner palace, relying greatly on favor.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong acceded, Shou was recalled as Right Vice Director and Academician of the Hall of Assembled Eminences, moving in and out of the inner palace and relying greatly on favor.

sentences.zh: 建白：「帝誕日，百官先詣光順門賀皇太后，然後上皇帝千萬歲壽。

translations.literal: He proposed: "On the emperor's birthday, the hundred officials should first go to Guangshun Gate to congratulate the empress dowager, and then offer the emperor wishes for ten thousand years of life.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed: "On the emperor's birthday, officials should first go to Guangshun Gate to congratulate the empress dowager, then offer the emperor wishes for ten thousand years of life.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: " The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 久之，宰相奏古無生日稱賀者，綬議格。

translations.literal: After a long while the chancellor memorialized that antiquity knew no birthday congratulations; Shou's proposal was rejected.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while the chancellor memorialized that antiquity knew no birthday congratulations; Shou's proposal was rejected.

sentences.zh: 時大臣論啟或未決，綬居中助可否。

translations.literal: When great ministers debated and matters were undecided, Shou stood in the middle and helped sway approval or rejection.
translations.idiomatic: When great ministers debated unresolved matters, Shou stood in the middle and helped sway approval or rejection.

sentences.zh: 九月九日宴群臣曲江，綬請集賢學士得別會，帝一順聽。

translations.literal: On the ninth day of the ninth month the emperor feasted the ministers at Qujiang; Shou requested that academicians of the Hall of Assembled Eminences hold a separate gathering, and the emperor readily assented.
translations.idiomatic: On the Double Ninth the emperor feasted ministers at Qujiang; Shou asked that academicians hold a separate gathering, and the emperor readily assented.

sentences.zh: 進位禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 帝問所以振災邀福者，對曰：「宋景公以善言退法星三舍，漢文除秘祝，敕有司祭而不祈，此二君皆受自至之福，書美前史。

translations.literal: The emperor asked how to dispel disasters and invite blessings; he replied: "Duke Jing of Song with good words made the punishing star retreat three lodges; Emperor Wen of Han abolished secret prayers and ordered officials to sacrifice without praying—both rulers received blessings that came of themselves, and the histories praise them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked how to dispel disasters and invite blessings; he replied: "Duke Jing of Song with good words made the punishing star retreat three lodges; Emperor Wen abolished secret prayers and ordered officials to sacrifice without praying—both received blessings that came of themselves, and the histories praise them.

sentences.zh: 如失德以卻災，媚神以丐助，神而有知，且因以譴也。

translations.literal: If one lacks virtue yet seeks to avert disaster, or flatters the spirits to beg help, should the spirits have knowledge they would instead send reproof.
translations.idiomatic: If one lacks virtue yet seeks to avert disaster, or flatters the spirits to beg help, should the spirits have knowledge they would instead send reproof.

sentences.zh: 」時帝不德，故托諷焉。

translations.literal: " At the time the emperor lacked virtue, so Shou framed it as indirect admonition.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the emperor lacked virtue, so Shou framed it as indirect admonition.

sentences.zh: 俄以檢校戶部尚書為山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: Soon he was made acting Minister of Revenue and military governor of the Shanxi West circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made acting Minister of Revenue and military governor of the Shanxi West circuit.

sentences.zh: 入辭，請門戟十二以行，又乞賜錢二百萬，官子元弼太常丞，帝以舊恩許之。

translations.literal: On taking leave of audience he requested twelve gate halberds for his journey and also begged two million in cash and an appointment for his son Yuanbi as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; the emperor granted it out of old favor.
translations.idiomatic: On taking leave he requested twelve gate halberds for his journey, begged two million in cash, and an appointment for his son Yuanbi as Vice Director of Sacrifices; the emperor granted it out of old favor.

sentences.zh: 綬耄而貪，不能事軍政，綱維亂弛。

translations.literal: Shou was aged and greedy and could not attend to military administration; discipline fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Shou was aged and greedy and could not manage military affairs; discipline collapsed.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈尚書右僕射，帝遣中人吊其家。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and the emperor sent a palace attendant to console his household.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Right Vice Director; the emperor sent a palace attendant to console his household.

sentences.zh: 有司謚通醜，故吏以為言，改謬醜，不報，罷。

translations.literal: The relevant office gave the posthumous title Tongchou ("entirely ugly"); former subordinates spoke up, and it was changed to Miu Chou ("absurdly ugly"); no reply was issued, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant office gave the posthumous epithet "Entirely Ugly"; former subordinates protested, and it was changed to "Absurdly Ugly"; no reply was issued, and the matter was dropped.
